title: Jets' Garrett Wilson enters concussion protocol a week before 2026 NFL trade deadline - CBS Sports
description: Could Wilson's status as potential trade bait be impacted by entering the concussion protocol?
body:
Could Wilson's status as potential trade bait be impacted by entering the concussion protocol?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the the top playmakers who could be available at the 2026 NFL trade deadline is now in the concussion protocol. New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Wednesday that 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year wide receiver Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol. Wilson leads the Jets in targets (63), catches (43), receiving yards (527) and receiving touchdowns (3) this season, and his four-year, $130 million contract extension is set to kick in next season. It sounds inconceivable that the rebuilding Jets would part with a 26-year-old who has been one of the team's faces, but Wilson showed public signs of frustration in their loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins in Week 7. CBS cameras caught Wilson appearing to yell at quarterback Geno Smith and passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. After the game, Wilson said it was a constructive conversation. 
"We were collaborating," said Wilson, via ESPN. "I don't even think I was talking to Geno. I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive. That's what that was."  
Wilson wants to "make an impact" and it will be interesting to see if that will remain to be with the Jets, who are 2-6, long term with the Nov. 10 trade deadline looming. 
"Just trying to figure out how we can fix where we're at right now, wanting to get it in our hands and make a difference and try to win these games that we feel like we're a better team -- and we're not," Wilson said. "Like I've said before, I want it in my hands to try and make an impact. So that's all we were talking about, just putting it in our hands and how we can make that happen, being aggressive throughout and keeping ourselves out of those situations so we can win these games."

title: Lions' Jack Campbell issues statement updating condition after scary injury vs. Vikings - CBS Sports
description: The Lions linebacker says he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with his upper body follo
body:
The Lions linebacker says he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with his upper body following a scary collision against the Vikings
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury during the team's eventual Week 8 victory against the Minnesota Vikings. Following a tackle of tight end T.J. Hockenson, the 26-year-old was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field. He remained on his stomach for several minutes after the collision and was not seen moving while trainers attended to him.The Lions were initially mum on any updates regarding Campbell. On Monday, the team announced he was resting and recovering at a local hospital, but that preliminary indications were "positive." On Wednesday, Campbell issued a statement himself through the team and revealed that he has full movement in his lower body. He's continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. However, he said he remains "very optimistic," even though he knows "there's still work ahead."Read the full statement below: 
"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this.I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong. Jack Campbell"Anytime, especially being able to hear it from him, that means a lot. That's powerful in itself, more than hearing it from me or anybody else," Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Wednesday. "Those are his and his family's words, so that's powerful. I know that always helps to know that he's improving. Because at this point, that's all you're looking for, is just to know that he's improving. The status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way. It always is going to help."Campbell is in his fourth season with the Lions. The Iowa product was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft and signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL this past offseason.
In 2025, Campbell was named a First Team All-Pro and Pro Bowler after recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended.

title: Jacoby Brissett trade: Ravens strike deal for Cardinals QB amid injury crisis - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore is expected to acquire the veteran quarterback from Arizona after injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Hunt
body:
Baltimore is expected to acquire the veteran quarterback from Arizona after injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano decimated its depth chart
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Baltimore Ravens are adding another quarterback to lead a room that has been devastated by injuries, according to ESPN. Baltimore has agreed to trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend, and compensation has not been finalized. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery on his first pass attempt against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. It could potentially be a season-ending injury. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley, came in and suffered a season-ending turf toe injury, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the likely candidate to start the Ravens' Week 9 matchup against Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. However, he is also dealing with an ankle injury. Brissett has spent the past two seasons in Arizona. The Cardinals recently demoted him from starter to third-stringer after Gardner Minshew came in on Sunday, threw three touchdowns, and helped Arizona eliminate a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat the Dallas Cowboys in overtime, 33-30. Brissett completed 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards and one interception before being replaced.Brissett, who turns 34 next month, has completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games this season. CBS Sports Research points out that his 75.6 yards per game to star tight end Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). This is the second time he has been traded in his career, and the Ravens mark his seventh team.
While Brissett can't replace what Jackson brought to this Ravens offense, he is an experienced quarterback who has started 73 games (23-50) and thrown 86 more touchdowns than the rest of the Ravens' healthy quarterbacks combined. His 1.5% career interception percentage is also tied for second-lowest in NFL history behind Aaron Rodgers' 1.4%. Brissett is one of five quarterbacks in the past 365 days to throw for 4,000 yards and 25 touchdowns, joining a list that includes Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott. He also upgrades his own situation. Over the last calendar year, the Cardinals have allowed 32.6 points per game -- which is four points higher than any other team in the NFL. The Ravens have allowed 10 points fewer per game (22.6) in that same span. 
Baltimore sits in the basement of the AFC North at 4-4, but hope a veteran under center can propel the Ravens to a playoff spot.

title: Ranking college basketball's top five in-season tournaments for 2026-27 as multi-team event landscape shifts - CBS Sports
description: True bracket-style tournaments are more scarce now, but there are some big-time matchups on deck
body:
True bracket-style tournaments are more scarce now, but there are some big-time matchups on deck
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:31 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This year's multi-team event schedule in men's college basketball shows how nothing stays the same for long in college sports. Now in their third year, Players Era events stand above the pack for staging the most impactful tournaments on the scene.But even the Players Era is undergoing a significant change in 2026. Gone is last year's confusing 18-team format that left final round matchups up to a series of hard-to-follow tiebreakers. This year, there is a 16-team Players Era event and a separate eight-team Players Era event that will take place the week before.Both are loaded with quality teams and will feature normal bracket-style structures that will make them easier to follow. This should be a welcome change. It's not the only change to the November MTE scene.As the Players Era format gets simplified, the Battle 4 Atlantis has gone in an unorthodox direction. It still features eight teams, but the conventional bracket-style format has been scrapped for a much more confusing setup. It includes two separate four-team pools. The "Signature Series" includes four pre-determined matchups involving Virginia, Marquette, Texas A&M and Xavier. There won't be a bracket-style format in the "Signature Series."
Alternately, the "Championship Bracket" of the Battle 4 Atlantis is an actual 4-team tournament with the winner of Memphis vs. Penn State advancing to play the winner of Wake Forest vs. Mississippi State. No one in either bracket will play a third game.In hopes of cutting through the clutter, we've distilled MTE season down to a ranking of the five best bracket-style events. The Battle 4 Atlantis misses the cut because of its wonky configuration.
        
            
                Grading college basketball debuts: First impressions of LSU's Will Wade, UNC, top transfers, 5-star freshmen
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
1. Players Era 16Dates: Nov. 24-28Location: Las VegasMatchups: Bracket 1: Miami vs. TCU, Creighton vs. Michigan, Baylor vs. Alabama, Gonzaga vs. Kansas State; Bracket 2: Tennessee vs. Maryland, San Diego State vs. Iowa State, Texas Tech vs. Louisville, Oregon vs. St. John's | Winners of each eight-team bracket play each other in a championship game
Breakdown: The Players Era 16 consists of 14 teams from high-major conferences and two Pac-12 powers in Gonzaga and San Diego State. Among them are nine of the top 20 teams from the preseason AP Top 25 poll. Potential second-round matchups include Miami vs. Michigan, Alabama vs. Gonzaga, Tennessee vs. Iowa State and St. John's vs. either Texas Tech or Louisville.This is going to be electric. Everyone is guaranteed three games, and it's a virtual certainty that each opportunity will be a potential resume-builder. Outside of Kansas State, all 16 teams began the season within the top 100 at KenPom.com. The winners of each eight-team bracket will square off in a fourth game for the chance to claim the Players Era 16 championship.
2. Players Era 8Dates: Nov. 17-19Location: Las VegasMatchups: Houston vs. Rutgers, Florida vs. Notre Dame, Kansas vs. UNLV, West Virginia vs. Auburn | Eight-team bracket style
Breakdown: The Players Era 8 is headlined by preseason No. 1 Florida and also includes Big 12 powers Houston and Kansas. Potential semifinal games include Houston vs. Florida and Kansas vs. Auburn. A couple of the first-round games (Houston vs. Rutgers and Florida vs. Notre Dame) look like potential blowouts. But this is a solid 8-team undercard to the Players Era 16. A title game bout between Florida and Kansas would be particularly captivating, but an all-Big 12 championship game between the Jayhawks and Houston is also a possibility if the Gators get tripped up.
3. Maui InvitationalDates: Nov. 23-25Location: Lahaina, HawaiiMatchups: Ole Miss vs. Clemson, Washington vs. BYU, VCU vs. Providence, Colorado State vs. Arizona | Eight-team bracket styleBreakdown: The event isn't what it used to be, as the Players Era has siphoned off many of the nation's top teams. But this year's Maui Invitational field is better than last year's. A year ago, just two of the eight teams went on to make the NCAA Tournament, and both of them (Texas and NC State) barely got in. With Arizona and a strong BYU team headlining this year's field, there is strong potential for interesting matchups throughout the bracket. A VCU vs. Providence showdown in the first round is particularly compelling as it's the sort of game that could resonate for months to come as both teams seek to build at-large cases for the Big Dance.
4. Rady Children's InvitationalDates: Nov. 26-27Location: San DiegoMatchups: Texas vs. Georgetown, UCLA vs. Saint Mary's | Four-team bracket styleBreakdown: The Rady Children's Invitational is just a four-team event, but it features a bracket-style format that could lead to a title-game showdown between Texas and UCLA. Both were preseason Top 25 teams full of intriguing talent. The Longhorns have bolstered their roster in a significant way for coach Sean Miller's second season by adding five-star freshmen Marcus Spears Jr. and Austin Goosby, in addition to star transfers David Punch (TCU) and Isaiah Johnson (Colorado). UCLA showed its mettle on the season's opening night by taking down Arizona. Coach Mick Cronin supplemented a strong nucleus of returners with Texas Tech transfer Jaylen Petty and European import Nikola Kusturica to give the Bruins the talent required to be a factor in the Big Ten title race.
5. Baha Mar Hoops Bahamas ChampionshipDates: Nov. 19-20Location: Nassau, BahamasMatchups: NC State vs. Murray State, Wisconsin vs. Seton Hall | Four-team bracket style
Breakdown: The Baha Mar Hoops Bahamas Championship stands out for being an actual tournament — albeit just a four-team tournament — at a time when many other MTEs have gone to formats consisting exclusively of set matchups. Murray State takes on NC State in a battle between one of the most high-octane and well-funded mid-major programs and an upstart ACC program under first-year coach Justin Gainey. The winner will get either Seton Hall or Wisconsin in the title game. The Pirates have designs on getting back to the NCAA Tournament after missing out with a 21-12 record last season. Wisconsin is the tournament's top brand, but the Badgers will have their hands full with Seton Hall and whichever opponent comes next.

Darnold will sit with a quad injury, while Lock is expected to make his second start of the season despite dealing with an elbow issue.

        Quarterback Sam Darnold will miss the Seattle Seahawks' Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals due to a quad injury, coach Mike Macdonald told reporters. Drew Lock will make his second start of the season in his place. Lock is also dealing with an elbow injury, which will be monitored throughout the week. Seattle has Jalen Milroe as Lock's backup. "He's able to throw. How much, we're working through that right now," Macdonald said about Lock.The Seahawks are coming off a 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night in which Darnold completed 17 of his 34 pass attempts for 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception.Lock started one game earlier this season when Darnold was sidelined by the soft-tissue injury suffered during the Week 1 victory against the New England Patriots. Coincidentally, that start also came against the Cardinals in Arizona. Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-7 victory. The Seahawks out-gained the Cardinals, 381 yards to 151 yards, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 155 yards and three touchdowns.
Darnold has not played well since Seattle's Super Bowl run last season. He's 3-4 as the starter, averaging just 211 passing yards per game, and has thrown 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions. Darnold's 23 interceptions since 2025 are tied for most in the NFL, and his -0.67 EPA per dropback when pressured ranks last in the NFL. When this news broke, CBS Sports analyst and former NFL quarterback Ben DiNucci said that Lock actually may give the 4-4 Seahawks a better chance to win this game.

title: Miami WR Malachi Toney injures ankle in practice, status unknown vs. Notre Dame - CBS Sports
description: The Hurricanes biggest weapon has an ankle injury heading into Miami's biggest game of the year
body:
The Hurricanes biggest weapon has an ankle injury heading into Miami's biggest game of the year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The No. 1 ranked Miami Hurricanes got some concerning injury news on Wednesday when star receiver Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice. Sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that the hope is the injury isn't serious and he has not been ruled out for Saturday's game yet but is still being evaluated. Toney is the Hurricanes biggest offensive weapon with 73 catches, 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season, and his production for the nation's top team has made him one of the Heisman Trophy favorites alongside his quarterback, Darian Mensah. Losing Toney the week of Miami's biggest game would be a disaster for the Hurricanes, but even if he's able to go but he's limited in any way it will make life that much more difficult for the Miami offense to create explosive plays against a talented Notre Dame defense. Toney's importance to the Miami offenseLast year's win over Notre Dame was Toney's breakout performance as a freshman, as he caught six passes for 82 yards and one touchdown in Miami's 27-24 victory to open the season. Toney is the top threat the Irish have to game-plan and account for with multiple defenders, and any limitations on his ability to get downfield or move in space would be a significant loss for Miami. 
Toney accounts for 35.1% of Miami's receptions, 38.6% of receiving yards and 46.4% of receiving touchdowns this season. Cooper Barkate is second on the team in all of those categories with 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns, and while talented, doesn't provide the same dynamic as Toney.The Hurricanes use Toney in myriad ways, and his ability to move around formations and alignments allows Shannon Dawson to attack different soft spots of defenses and prevents easy adjustments to what Miami is doing because of their variation. If Toney isn't as dynamic (or isn't in the lineup), it allows the defense to focus more on slowing down Miami's run game. The Hurricanes are 21st in the country in rushing offense at 202.5 yards per game and are 10th in yards per attempt at 5.49. Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory make up one of the nation's best running back tandems, but they're made all the more effective by the respect defenses have to give to the big-play threat the passing game always presents when Toney is on the field. 
Notre Dame's defense figured to face the difficult choice of sending more bodies into the box to slow the run or keep help over the top to prevent Toney from getting loose. If Toney isn't as effective or cannot play, the ripple effects extend well beyond the Hurricanes' passing game. Heisman Trophy implicationsBeyond the impact Toney's injury could have on Miami's biggest game of the season, Saturday's game against Notre Dame figured to be Toney (and Mensah's) best opportunity to author a Heisman moment on a big national stage. Toney was second in the Heisman Trophy odds coming into the week at +290 at FanDuel Sportsbook -- only trailing Mensah at +170. After the injury news was reported on Wednesday, Toney dropped all the way to +800, which is now fourth on the odds sheet. Toney's injury could also impact Darian Mensah's Heisman chances, as his passing productivity would likely take a hit if his best receiver can't play or is limited. 
As a result, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is back to the top spot in the odds at +170, Mensah has slipped a touch to +200, and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr jumps to +700 as the Irish have moved out to a 6.5-point favorite over the Hurricanes. CBS Sports will continue to provide updates on Toney's status as the week progresses and more information becomes available.

title: Predicting the full 14-team NFL playoff bracket entering Week 9: Bears make Super Bowl run - CBS Sports
description: Are the Bears the best team in the NFC? Our latest playoff projection answers that question
body:
Are the Bears the best team in the NFC? Our latest playoff projection answers that question
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the NFL season heading into its halfway point this week, I have some good news for everyone: All 32 teams are still mathematically alive to make the playoffs. And yes, that means even the Titans and Chargers could still make the postseason. I'm guessing they won't, but they could, and that's what matters here.Heading into Week 9, this is when we finally start to see the contenders separate themselves from the pretenders. But who are the real contenders? Who's actually going to make the playoffs? Glad you asked. To help us figure that out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 151 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.  With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.       
     Projected AFC playoff field     The AFC playoff projection underwent some massive changes this week. The Broncos turned the AFC West upside down with their win over the Chiefs. Thanks to that victory, our model now projects that Denver ends up winning the division title for the second straight year. Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record):      1. Bills (6-1) -- AFC East champion      2. Jaguars (5-2) -- AFC South champion      3. Broncos (6-2) -- AFC West champion      4. Bengals (5-2) -- AFC North champion      5. Chiefs (5-2)      6. Steelers (6-2)      7. Patriots (5-3)  JUST MISSED: Texans (2-5), Browns (5-3) If the Broncos win the AFC West, the Chiefs will enter the playoffs as a wild-card team, which has never happened in Patrick Mahomes' career. Since he took over the starting job in 2018, the Chiefs have made the playoffs a total of seven times, and all of those came after a season where Kansas City won the division. The Chiefs have been so good with Mahomes that they've NEVER played a road game in the wild card round with him at quarterback, but we could see that happen this year.
       Projected NFC playoff field       For the third time this season, we have a new team projected to win the NFC North. The Bears have taken over the top spot after their dominating win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Over the past eight weeks, we've seen the Vikings and Lions both projected to win the division, but heading into Week 9, our computer likes Da' Bears.   Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record):      1. 49ers (6-1) -- NFC West champion      2. Bears (6-2) -- NFC North champion      3. Giants (4-2-1) -- NFC East champion      4. Buccaneers (3-5) -- NFC South champion      5. Vikings (4-2)      6. Lions (4-3)      7. Seahawks (5-2)   JUST MISSED: Packers (5-3), Rams (4-4) For the first time in NFL history, we could have a situation where TWO teams win their division despite not being over .500. Right now, our projection has the Giants winning the NFC East with a record of 8-8-1 and the Buccaneers winning the NFC South at 8-9. The Bucs started the season 0-4, but our computer loves them after watching Tampa Bay destroy two division rivals -- the Panthers and Falcons -- in consecutive weeks. 
There have been seasons where two teams have gotten in the playoffs at .500 or worse, but it's always involved at least one wild card team. For instance, the Commanders won the NFC East with a 7-9 record in 2020 while the Bears got in as a wild card team with an 8-8 record. However, there has never been a situation where two divisional winners both finish .500 or worse. If that happens, the biggest losers will be the Packers and Rams, both being projected to miss the playoffs despite finishing above .500.        Wild card round       AFC       (2) Jaguars 27-20 over (7) Patriots. The last time these two teams met in the postseason, the Jags lost a controversial game in the AFC Championship. This time around, the Jags get their revenge. Jacksonville beat the Patriots 35-6 back in Week 3, and although this game is much closer, the Jags still get the win.     (3) Broncos 21-19 over (6) Steelers. The last time the Broncos won the Super Bowl back in 2015, they started their playoff run with a win over the Steelers, so this could start to feel like deja vu for fans in Denver. These two teams will actually face each other on Black Friday, so we'll get to see them battle in the regular season before a possible playoff game in January.  (4) Bengals 26-25 over (5) Chiefs. If there's one quarterback who has had some major success against Patrick Mahomes, it's Joe Burrow. Not only did he lead the Bengals to a win in the 2021 AFC title game, but Burrow is 2-0 all-time against the Chiefs at home, and he continues that streak with another win here. NFC       (2) Bears 24-21 over (7) Seahawks. These two teams just met on Monday night with the Bears destroying the Seahawks on the road in Seattle. This time around, the Seahawks keep it closer, but they can't quite figure out how to stop Ben Johnson's offense. (6) Lions 29-23 over (3) Giants. The Lions have never won a road playoff game in the Super Bowl era (0-12), but they end that drought here with a win against an overmatched Giants team.       (4) Buccaneers 21-17 over (5) Vikings. The Buccaneers make history in this game by becoming the first NFC team ever to overcome a 0-4 start to make the playoffs. The Bucs then use their strong rushing attack to run over Minnesota's defense. With the loss, the Vikings' 6-0 start goes to waste, and Minnesota is forced to spend another offseason looking for a quarterback. And now, we're down to our final eight teams.               Divisional round       AFC       (1) Bills 34-24 over (4) Bengals. The Bills come out on fire after their bye week and knock off the Bengals in what would be the team's first playoff game at their new stadium. This would definitely be an interesting matchup, and that's because Joe Burrow is 2-1 all-time against Josh Allen. (2) Jaguars 21-19 over (3) Broncos. The Jaguars' first divisional playoff win ever came back in 1996 against the Broncos, and history repeats itself here with the Jaguars knocking off Denver again. This game ends up as a back-and-forth thriller that's decided by a Cam Little field goal late in the fourth quarter. NFC       (1) 49ers 28-27 over (6) Lions. Three years ago, the Lions blew a 24-7 lead against the 49ers in the NFC title game. They finally get their shot at revenge here, but they come up short. Brock Purdy out-duels Jared Goff and ends up leading the 49ers to their fifth NFC title game over the past eight seasons. (2) Bears 28-19 over (4) Buccaneers. These two teams are actually playing THIS WEEK on Sunday night in Chicago, so we'll be getting a possible preview of what a playoff game might look like. The Bucs' defense has been strong this season, but in our playoff game, it can't slow down Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. With a win here, the Bears advance to their first NFC title game since 2010. If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Jaguars) and two teams that haven't won a Super Bowl in over 30 years. The 49ers' last title came in 1994, while the Bears haven't won a Lombardi Trophy since 1985, when they won their first and only Super Bowl.        Conference title games       AFC Championship       (1) Bills 28-24 over (2) Jaguars. Last year, the Jaguars' season ended with a painful playoff loss to the Bills, and unfortunately for Jacksonville, they lost to Buffalo for the second straight year. With Josh Allen aiming to get to his first Super Bowl, he takes over the game and leads the Bills to a tight win. NFC Championship       (2) Bears 26-24 over (1) 49ers. With two offensive gurus going at it in Kyle Shanahan and Ben Johnson, this game could come down to who plays better defense, and right now, the Bears have the advantage on that side of the ball. title: Robert Kraft named one of five contributor nominees for 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class - CBS Sports
description: The Patriots owner is one of five contributor nominees still under consideration after falling short of induction
body:
The Patriots owner is one of five contributor nominees still under consideration after falling short of induction in the previous Hall of Fame cycle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Patriots owner Robert Kraft is one of five contributor nominees for the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class, it was announced Wednesday. The Contributor Subcommittee whittled the field down from 42 options to five, and it will meet again on Nov. 17 to decide on one of the five remaining nominees to advance to the full Selection Committee. The Selection Committee will then announce its selections for the 2027 class shortly before the Super Bowl.Kraft is joined by Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten.Kraft received the subcommittee's vote last year to advance to the Selection Committee vote, but he was controversially left out of the 2026 Hall of Fame class. Kraft has been eligible for the Hall of Fame for years, but last year was the first time he had advanced out of the subcommittee. Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick, in his first year on the ballot, did not get selected for the Hall of Fame, either.Kraft, 85, has owned the Patriots since 1994. Under his ownership, New England has won six Super Bowls and appeared in five more, including last season's loss to the Seahawks. Prior to Kraft's ownership, the Patriots had only been to one Super Bowl, which it lost. In addition, Kraft has been a key member of several NFL committees, and he helped lead the creation of Gillette Stadium, which opened in 2002.In 2024, ESPN detailed Kraft's long struggle for a spot in Canton, with various voters pointing to Spygate (when the Patriots taped the Jets' practices), Deflategate and dismissed charges after Kraft's two visits to a Jupiter, Florida, massage parlor as reasons why Kraft hasn't been inducted.
As for the other nominees:Hay owned the Canton Bulldogs from 1918-22 and was integral in creating the NFL.McCaskey owned the Bears from 1983-2025. She was the daughter of Bears founder George Halas.Williams was the first Black quarterback to win a Super Bowl, leading Washington to a victory over Denver in 1988 with 340 passing yards and four touchdowns.Wooten played 10 seasons as an offensive lineman before getting into scouting and player personnel roles. He also chaired the Fritz Pollard Alliance.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Latest deals, grades as Jacoby Brissett heads to Baltimore - CBS Sports
description: Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Chicago's blockbuster addition of Jeffery Simmo
body:
Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Chicago's blockbuster addition of Jeffery Simmons and the Colts' trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A steady stream of blockbuster moves in advance of the 2026 NFL trade deadline redistributed some of the league's top talent at numerous positions. Even more impactful transactions could be on the way before Nov. 10, but in the meantime, the Chicago Bears are the biggest winners of the deadline thus far with their highly fruitful acquisition of Jeffery Simmons, while the Indianapolis Colts emerged as the most aggressive sellers in dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.Trade watch continues for a myriad of stars on struggling teams, including Jonathan Taylor, Khalil Mack, George Pickens and others. At the same time, teams battling for position at the front of the postseason race must decide how much to invest in those standouts who are available on the trade market.There is only one more week of games until the trade deadline, so this year's contenders and pretenders are about as clear as they will be before it is too late to buy and sell. It is safe to expect a flurry of moves in the coming days as those franchises gear up for the home stretch or look ahead to the future.Below is every in-season trade ahead of the NFL's 2026 deadline.Nov. 4: Ravens add another QB amid injury crisisRavens receive: Jacoby Brissett, TBDCardinals receive: TBDBaltimore has agreed to trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, with a deal expected to be completed by this weekend. The compensation has not yet been announced. 
This was expected from the Ravens, because their quarterback situation went from bad to worse on Sunday. The highly anticipated return of starter Lamar Jackson lasted just one play. Jackson suffered a thumb injury and is now placed on IR. Tyler Huntley, who started in place of Jackson, took over but also went down. He is reportedly out for the season with a turf toe injury. The team relied on emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano to finish the game, but he is also dealing with an ankle injury. In order to avoid the scare of a running back having to sub in as quarterback, they now have another option. Brissett has spent the last two seasons with the Cardinals. Oct. 29: Bears go all-in, acquire Jeffery SimmonsBears receive: Jeffery Simmons, 2028 fifth-round pickTitans receive: 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pickIn giving up two first-rounders to secure a perennial All-Pro defensive tackle, the Bears went all-in and opened their Super Bowl contention window. The transaction paid immediate dividends when Simmons logged a sack and led the team with six tackles in his Chicago debut: A commanding 34-17 road win over the Seahawks. Mortgaging so much of their future first-round capital showed that the Bears trust their roster, as currently constructed, to compete at the top of the league, and Simmons is the kind of game-changing talent worth the steep price. His production in the pass rush and in run defense could help Chicago maximize its high-octane unit on the other side of the ball led by Caleb Williams.
This move sends the Titans deeper into their rebuild. Questions lie ahead about whether to stick with Cam Ward at quarterback, and with the first-round picks they acquired from dealing Simmons, there will be curiosity as to whether they will use one to land a new signal-caller. Regardless of how they use the picks, moving on from one of the greatest players in franchise history shows how bleak the present is in Tennessee and that all eyes are on the future.Trade grades:Bears: A- | Titans: C+Oct. 27: DeForest Buckner reunites with 49ers49ers receive: DeForest BucknerColts receive: 2027 fourth-round pickThe seemingly nonstop onslaught of injuries hit the 49ers' defensive line, resulting in CJ West landing on injured reserve with a bone chip in his knee and Alfred Collins being ruled out for the year with a torn patellar tendon. That heightened the need for immediate help in the trenches, so the 49ers brought Buckner back after his six-plus years in Indianapolis. The 49ers selected Buckner in the first round of the 2016 draft, and the best years of his prime came during his time in San Francisco, so this is a welcome return for someone the franchise remembers fondly. Buckner remains one of the NFL's top pass-rushing interior defensive linemen and will aid in the 49ers' Super Bowl push.Buckner's exit marked the second trade in one day for the slumping Colts, who are in the midst of tearing things down with multiple star players on the move and former general manager Chris Ballard out the door. There is an argument to be made that a Day 3 pick was an underwhelming return, but for a 32-year-old veteran on an expiring contract, the Colts were content to get at least something of value for a player who was likely to leave in free agency anyway. Buckner grew publicly frustrated with Indianapolis' struggles, which heightened the anticipation for his trade or an eventual departure at the end of his contract.
Trade grades:49ers: A | Colts: B+Oct. 27: Seahawks bolster offensive line with Quenton NelsonSeahawks receive: Quenton NelsonColts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pickSeahawks general manager Jon Schneider is keen to make big-time moves ahead of the trade deadline. This is the fourth consecutive year in which Seattle made a play for an impactful midseason addition to its roster. Nelson is as stellar of an offensive lineman as there is on the trade market this year as a six-time All-Pro and should elevate a struggling Seahawks run game over the long term, even if his arrival did not deliver an immediate boost in the loss to the Bears in his debut. This is also a savvy transaction for the front office given that it stands to receive at least one compensatory third-round pick in 2027; trading a third-rounder for Nelson was thus an easy price to pay.The Colts got more in return for Nelson than they did for Buckner, which is to be expected considering his status as perhaps the top interior lineman in football. This is still a discount, though, and they remain without a first-round pick in either of the next two drafts. If they can use the third-rounder and next year's fifth-rounder to move up in the order, the trade deadline sale could prove more worthwhile.Trade grades:Seahawks: A | Colts: C+Oct. 11: Texans take a shot on Marvin Harrison Jr.Texans receive: Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 seventh-round pickCardinals receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pickHarrison reunited with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, upon his arrival in Houston. Will that help him rekindle what has become a disappointing career? His first two games with the Texans were mostly underwhelming, but he did haul in a touchdown reception in Week 7 and could secure a more sizable target share as the team seeks for a go-to No. 2 option behind star pass-catcher Nico Collins. This is trending toward a lost season for the Texans, but they will have another year of control over Harrison and the option to pick up a fifth year in 2028. If they can mold him into the star he was supposed to become out of Ohio State, their passing game will be in excellent shape over the long haul.
Trading Harrison was an admission that he was a bust of a former first-round pick, but to get a second-rounder in the process and to upgrade with a Day 3 pick swap was about as good of a deal as the Cardinals could have landed. Harrison ran his course in the desert and was clearly a poor fit in Mike LaFleur's system, so maximizing his value in the trade was a big win for a team that is not going to contend for anything meaningful in 2026 anyway.Trade grades:Texans: C- | Cardinals: B+Oct. 7: Ravens land Cam JurgensRavens receive: Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pickEagles receive: 2028 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pickThe interior offensive line in Baltimore was a glaring issue last year and into the start of 2026. The Jurgens trade addressed that head-on. Not only did the Ravens find their long-term replacement for Tyler Linderbaum, who left in free agency, but the addition also allowed them to move Olaivavega Ioane from center back to right guard. The full benefits of this move may not show up until Lamar Jackson returns to action, whether that be later in 2026 or next season.On the Eagles' side, Jurgens' exit effectively marked the end of an era for a once-legendary offensive line that also saw longtime tackle Lane Johnson and legendary position coach Jeff Stoutland enter retirement. It is a turning of the page and one that netted a couple of draft picks for a franchise that now looks destined to rebuild following a six-game losing streak. Philadelphia had been playing Jurgens out of position, anyway.
Trade grades:Ravens: B+ | Eagles: B-Oct. 1: Joey Porter Jr. brings much-needed help to Cowboys defenseCowboys receive: Joey Porter Jr.Steelers receive: 2028 second-round pick, conditional 2027 sixth-round pick (vested)If Porter cannot fix the Cowboys' defense, then that unit might be broken beyond repair in 2026. Dallas made a splash to address its greatest weakness and has thus far seen the exact kind of individual impact it envisioned from the star cornerback, as he allowed a diminutive 39.6 passer rating and just three completions on 11 targets across his first four games with the team. Still, the unit around him is in shambles. And with Porter set to reach unrestricted free agency this offseason, this could be a one-year rental that fails to produce a postseason appearance.The Steelers made it clear that they were not going to shell out market-resetting money to keep Porter around on a long-term contract extension. By declining to meet his demands as he sat out the start of the season, they only had one viable option, which was to trade him. A first-round pick would have been the preferable return package, but Pittsburgh received the next-best thing with both a second-rounder and 2027 draft capital. That sixth-round pick in next year's draft already vested, as it was conditional upon Porter being active for just two games with the Cowboys.Trade grades:Cowboys: C | Steelers: B-Sept. 28: Giants find replacement QB in J.J. McCarthyGiants receive: J.J. McCarthyVikings receive: 2027 fifth-round pickThe torn knee ligaments Jaxson Dart sustained in Week 2 made the Giants desperate for quarterback help, because the rest of the roster remained talented enough to compete for the NFC East crown. The McCarthy acquisition at first came across as puzzling given his own struggles to stay healthy, his underwhelming play when available and the fact that New York already has a franchise quarterback and thus has little to gain from McCarthy potentially developing into a viable starter. But it has aged better than expected. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter in Week 6, earned the starting job over Jameis Winston and promptly delivered a road win over the Texans to place the Giants in command of the division.
Getting anything in return for McCarthy after a disastrous start to his career was a win for the Vikings. He slipped all the way down to the third line of Minnesota's depth chart behind a couple of low-ceiling veterans in Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz and was clearly no longer part of the franchise's plans.Trade grades:Giants: C | Vikings: B+

title: MLB rumors: The only Oriole not on the trading block, Rays' Drew Rasmussen plan and Astros add to manager hunt - CBS Sports

body:
Here are the latest MLB trade and free agency rumors for Wednesday, Nov. 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026

    2:49 pm ET

        The Brewers have now been World Series champions for just one week (minus a few hours) and they should still be basking in the glory for quite a while. As the offseason marches on, the next big date will be Nov. 17, when decisions on qualifying offers are due from the eight players who received one. In the meantime, the rumor mill should be ever-so-slowly churning. We'll round it up here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Astros to interview Pujols for manager openingThe Houston Astros moved on from general manager Dana Brown in August and fired manager Joe Espada after the 2026 season. Newly hired general manager Randy Flores is now tasked with landing a new dugout boss, and a three-time MVP and future Hall of Famer is in the mix. The Astros will interview Albert Pujols for the manager job this week, per The Athletic.Pujols has long made it known that he desires to be an MLB manager. He recently interviewed for vacancies with the Padres and Angels (both last offseason) and he also managed the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic this past spring. It should be further noted that Pujols is in the fourth year of a 10-year, $100 personal services contract with the Angels that was part of the mega-deal he signed with them as a player prior to the 2012 season as a player. 
Other known candidates for the Astros manager job are Rangers bench coach Luis Urueta and Yankees bench coach (not to mention former Tigers and Angels manager) Brad Ausmus. Former Astros third baseman Morgan Ensberg, the manager of the Triple-A Rays affiliate Durham Bulls, will also interview this week, according to MLB.com.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orioles looking to deal for SP and OF helpThe Orioles are willing to listen to trade offers on any player other than Pete Alonso as they seek both rotation and outfield help, according to The Baltimore Banner. The  Orioles reportedly aren't "actively shopping" any players, but they are looking for upgrades at starting pitcher and outfielder and realize one of the ways that could happen is via a trade. Surely they wouldn't sell low on Gunnar Henderson, given his immense upside, so we can probably take him off the table unless some team makes it worth their while. There is a glut of infielders, though. With Alonso at first base and Henderson at short, they have Jackson Holliday, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Jordan Westburg and Coby Mayo for two spots. Even using one of the four at designated hitter, it's easy to see where a deal could happen. 
Westburg and Encarnacion-Strand are under team control through 2029 while Holliday is controlled through 2030 and Mayo through 2031. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rays want to keep RasmussenThe American League champion Rays recently picked up the $20 million club option on All-Star starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen. That would be a franchise-record salary for one player in a single season. It might seem odd to exercise an option and then deal a player to an outsider, but locking Rasmussen in for a one-year deal makes him an attractive trade candidate instead of just letting him walk in free agency, and this is how the Rays generally operate. We've seen it so many times: they get ahead of losing guys to free agency, sometimes even dealing them a year or two earlier. They've done it with Randy Arozarena, Isaac Paredes, Tyler Glasnow and even going back to franchise legends like David Price, Evan Longoria and Ben Zobrist. The Rays right now are saying they intend to keep Rasmussen for 2027."Not a declarative this, that, whatever, but I can sit here very confidently and say that every intention right now is thinking about Ras anchoring our rotation and how to make this team better going into next year," club president Erik Neander said on Tuesday, via the Tampa Bay Times.
If they want to contend again next year, it sure seems like they need Rasmussen, with Nick Martinez and Freddy Peralta off to free agency. That leaves Rasmussen atop the rotation, followed by Shane McClanahan, Griffin Jax, Ryan Pepiot and a bunch of question marks. There are questions attached to McClanahan, Jax and Pepiot too.

Milton will replace Tanner McKee and become Philadelphia's third starting quarterback of the season when the Eagles face the NFC East-leading Giants
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:41 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles are entrusting a former Dallas Cowboy to be their new starting quarterback. Joe Milton will be the team's starting quarterback in Week 9 against the NFC East-leading New York Giants, per ESPN. Milton will be the third Eagles starting quarterback this season after Jalen Hurts went on injured reserve and backup Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts. The Eagles scooped him up off of the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16, a day before Hurts went on IR. "I think he's worked really hard," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday morning, via NBC Sports Philadelphia. "Him and [quarterbacks coach] Parks [Frazier] have spent a ton of time together, getting him caught up to speed. I know the developmental periods; those always help to be able to run our plays. But he works extremely hard. He is always in the building, doing the extra things. I like his progression."  
Milton could bring the deep ball back to the Eagles' offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre. However, Schottenheimer also expressed reservations about Milton's game, particularly his accuracy and touch. That's why Sam Howell won the Dallas backup job, leaving Milton as Dallas' No. 3 quarterback on the practice squad and up for grabs for Philadelphia to scoop him up. The Cowboys originally acquired Milton, a 2024 sixth-round pick, in April of 2025 in a trade with the New England Patriots, and he served as Dak Prescott's backup in 2025. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in both areas when the lights came on in Dallas' three exhibition games: he completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating.
"I'm going to say that the upside, I'm not going to say you put him into a box of what he could be, but the arm talent's real," Schottenheimer said in camp. "I think we've talked a lot in here about the touch and how he's developed the touch. I do know that he did a much better job with our system. This is what guys that come from that spread system [in college] have to deal with in terms of the learning curve of coming in and having to learn how to huddle, call a play in the huddle and make different decisions. ... I think about that. ... So again, I think Joe's going to be a terrific player in this league. I'm not going to say in what regard, but like I said, it was a very tough decision."

title: Agent's Take: What's next between Lamar Jackson, Ravens after yet another injury - CBS Sports
description: Jackson's contract with the Ravens expires after the 2027 season, but can he and Baltimore reach an agreement bef
body:
Jackson's contract with the Ravens expires after the 2027 season, but can he and Baltimore reach an agreement before then? What happens if they can't?
        
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        Lamar Jackson's return against the Buffalo Bills from a three-game absence after a high ankle sprain was very short-lived --  one offensive play, to be exact. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback injured his thumb in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills when his right hand hit edge rusher Greg Rousseau on the follow-through of a pass attempt. Jackson is out indefinitely after being placed on injured reserve as his right thumb requires surgery.The potential season-ending thumb injury raises questions about Jackson's future in Baltimore. Jackson is in the fourth year of a five-year deal that made him the NFL's highest-paid player at the time, with $52 million per year after being designated as a non-exclusive franchise player. During the 2027 contract year, Jackson is scheduled to earn an unsecured $52 million, consisting of a $51.25 million base salary and a $750,000 workout bonus. His salary cap number is $84.34 million. More importantly, Jackson's contract contains a no-trade clause and another provision preventing the Ravens from designating him as a franchise or transition player when his contract expires following the 2027 season.
The $84.34 million cap hit is untenable. It is 2027's second-highest number behind Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes' $90.35 million, which will surely be lowered through a contract restructure. The Ravens have an NFL-high $366.74 million in 2027 cap commitments with 45 players under contract and a little less than $1.4 million in existing 2026 cap space that can be carried over to the 2027 league year, according to NFLPA data. The salary cap for 2027 should be between $322.5 million and $327.5 million, considering comparable growth after a 7.88% increase between 2025 and 2026.So, where does Jackson's contract currently stand, and what could be ahead? Let's take a look.Jackson holds most of the leverage right nowJackson seemingly controls his own destiny because of his contract situation. Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti wanted to extend Jackson's contract prior to the start of the 2026 league year in March. There are reports that Jackson, who represents himself and has never had an agent, was the hold-up. 
Instead, with a deal not done, the Ravens resorted to the backup plan. Jackson's contract was restructured to create $39.96 million of much-needed 2026 cap room, with a dummy/voiding 2030 contract year added for bonus proration purposes.Jackson still has significant negotiating leverage if he wants a new deal, thanks to those clauses in his contract and the exorbitant 2027 cap number, despite durability concerns. He's had various injuries throughout 2025 and 2026, including those affecting his hamstring, ankle, toe, knee, back, and thumb. Assuming Jackson is done for the year, he will have only appeared in 18 of a possible 34 regular season games over these two seasons. In the prior two seasons (2023 and 2024), Jackson only missed one game.Will injuries affect Jackson's negotiations?The thumb injury is a freak accident. Jackson seems poised for a big 2026 season in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system before the ankle injury. In the four games Jackson played prior to initially getting hurt, he completed 70.8% of his passes (68 of 96 attempts) for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception to post a 119.6 passer rating. He added 144 yards on the ground in 19 carries with one touchdown. 
The completion percentage is a career high, while the passer rating matches his season best from 2024. He was also on pace for career highs in yards per pass attempt (10.1) and yards per completion (14.2). The Ravens were tied for first in the AFC North with a 3-1 record.The lack of availability in recent years could give the Ravens some reservations about signing Jackson, who turns 30 in January, to another market-setting deal. However, none of the two-time NFL MVP's injuries can be considered career-threatening. The Chiefs didn't have any qualms about reworking Mahomes' contract in June to make him the NFL's highest-paid player even though he was coming off a more serious injury (torn ACL and LCL in his left knee) than any Jackson has ever had. Mahomes also set career lows with a 62.7% completion percentage and 89.6 passer rating, which ranked 23rd in the NFL, during the 2025 season. Plus, the Chiefs had a losing record at 6-11 for the first time since 2012. 
By adding two new years, Mahomes is under contract through 2033 for eight years, totaling $504.75 million (average $63.1 million per year). Let's look at some details of his contract for comparison:Mahomes' deal is worth up to $522.25 million, including base salary escalators and incentives. The deal includes $237 million in conventional guarantees, which is the cash in the first four contract years. Out of this $237 million, $150 million is fully guaranteed at signing. The $150 million fully guaranteed is the second most ever in an NFL contract. Mahomes' $63.1 million AAV raised the bar for quarterback salaries. It was a 5.16% increase over the four-year, $240 million contract extension (averaging $60 million per year) Dak Prescott received from the Dallas Cowboys in 2024.Could Jackson be open to a trade?Jackson's reported unwillingness to have serious contract discussions during the offseason has led to speculation that he may not want to stay in Baltimore. Trading Jackson has its own set of issues. The Ravens can't move Jackson without his consent because of the no-trade clause. 
Typically, trades for a starting quarterback occur before the NFL Draft, which is April 29 through May 1 in 2027. With a trade on this timeline, the Ravens would have $74.81 million of dead money, a salary cap charge for a player no longer on a team's roster. That's because of the salary conversion that took place earlier this year and because Jackson's contract was structured with two prorated option bonuses. That's only a $9.53 million cap savings from Jackson's 2027 cap hit. The record for dead money related to an individual player in one league year is quarterback Tua Tagovailoa's $55.4 million, due to the Miami Dolphins releasing him with a post-June 1 designation in March 2026.Jackson's hypothetical $74.81 million in dead money would consist of:$14.35 million prorated in 2027 from Jackson's signing bonus $7 million prorated from the first option bonus in 2024 relating to his 2027 contract year and dummy/voiding 2028 contract year$13.5 million prorated from the second option bonus in 2025 relating to his 2027 contract year, as well as dummy/voiding 2028 and 2029 contract years$39.96 million prorated from the contract restructure signing bonus in 2026 relating to his 2027 contract year and three dummy/voiding contract years running from 2028 through 2030In this situation, Jackson would be off Baltimore's books beginning in 2028. The optimal time for the Ravens to trade Jackson, salary cap-wise, is after June 1. By waiting until June 2, the bonus proration from Jackson's three dummy/voiding contract years wouldn't accelerate onto Baltimore's 2027 salary cap. It would be a 2028 cap charge. The $74.81 million would be split into $32.34 million of 2027 dead money and $42.47 million of 2028 dead money, meaning the Ravens pick up $52 million of 2027 cap space in the process.
There are two big drawbacks to a delayed trade. The Ravens would have to perform some salary cap gymnastics to carry Jackson's $84.34 million cap number until June. The acquiring team would want a much earlier timetable for a trade so Jackson could have as much time as possible to get acclimated to a new offense and develop chemistry with his wide receivers.Jackson's value in any potential tradeThe no-trade clause needing to be waived could impact Baltimore's return in exchange for Jackson. This dynamic will make it harder for the Ravens to leverage interest from teams into a haul comparable to the one the Houston Texans and Seattle Seahawks received for Deshaun Watson and Russell Wilson, respectively, in 2022. That would especially be the case if Jackson, a South Florida native, had a specific destination in mind, such as the Dolphins.Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick were dealt to the Cleveland Browns for: 2022, 2023, and 2024 first-round picks2022 fourth-round pick2023 third-round pick2024 fourth-round pickThe Denver Broncos acquired Wilson and a 2022 fourth-round pick from the Seahawks for:
Multiple players (tight end Noah Fant, defensive lineman Shelby Harris and quarterback Drew Lock)2022 and 2023 first-round picks2022 and 2023 second-round picks2022 fifth-round pickThe worst-case scenario for the Ravens should be receiving Jeffery Simmons-type compensation for Jackson. The Chicago Bears just acquired the All-Pro defensive tackle and a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick. Presumably, the acquiring team would be working out a new deal with Jackson in connection with the trade or shortly thereafter. It wouldn't make a lot of sense for Jackson to potentially just be a one-year rental after giving up substantial assets to acquire him.What if Jackson and the Ravens can't reach a dealThere isn't a lot the Ravens can do if Jackson is determined to become an unrestricted free agent in 2028 because of the clause prohibiting a franchise or transition tag after his contract expires. Keeping Jackson at his $84.34 million cap number would be unprecedented. The largest cap number a team has ever had during the regular season is held by the Cowboys, with Prescott at $50.5 million in 2025. The Ravens would have Jackson at essentially 67% more than Prescott's cap number by leaving his cap number intact.
Another contract restructure might be necessary. Depending upon how much of Jackson's base salary was converted into signing bonus, as much as $37.4 million of 2027 cap room could be created without adding a dummy/voiding 2031 contract year. A maximum contract restructure of base salary would create a cap nightmare for the Ravens in 2028 with Jackson signing elsewhere. Ravens would have $79.9 million in 2028 dead money due to Jackson's departure.There is a remote chance that a refusal to negotiate a contract extension and to waive the no-trade clause would lead to the once-unimaginable: Jackson getting his freedom one year early. Releasing Jackson with a post-June 1 designation next March 2027 would have the same cap implications as a trade after June 1. Jackson's full $84.34 million cap number would remain on Baltimore's books until June 2, when his $52 million salary would be removed, resulting in a corresponding gain of 2027 cap space. Baltimore would have $42.47 million in dead money in 2028. The major difference is that Jackson would be free to sign with another team upon his release, and the Ravens wouldn't qualify for a 2029 compensatory third-round pick like they would if he left with an expiring contract in 2028.
Joel Corry is a former sports agent who helped found Premier Sports & Entertainment, a sports management firm that represents professional athletes and coaches. Prior to his tenure at Premier, Joel worked for Management Plus Enterprises, which represented Shaquille O'Neal, Hakeem Olajuwon and Ronnie Lott.

title: CJ Carr faces defining moment as Notre Dame's CFP hopes ride on clash vs. Miami - CBS Sports
description: The Fighting Irish quarterback has struggled against ranked opponents, but Miami's vulnerable secondary offers th
body:
The Fighting Irish quarterback has struggled against ranked opponents, but Miami's vulnerable secondary offers the perfect stage to save Notre Dame's playoff hopes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When the College Football Playoff rankings were released on Tuesday, Notre Dame was one of the biggest losers in the field. The Fighting Irish sit at No. 11 with only one loss against No. 9 BYU, but without quality wins to their name. One year after finishing as the first team out of the College Football Playoff, the Fighting Irish are firmly on the bubble. Notre Dame projects as the last team in and can't afford any more slip-ups.Now, a Saturday matchup against No. 1 Miami becomes a must-win game. And more importantly, it marks the most important game of quarterback CJ Carr's career. Carr has been one of the steadiest quarterbacks in college football, completing 67% of his passes with an 18-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. His 82.7 QBR is eighth-best in college football, adjusted for competition. But in the Fighting Irish's lone quality matchup against the Cougars, Carr was lackluster. 
The junior completed only 55% of his passes -- 27-for-49 -- the lowest completion percentage of his career on the most pass attempts in his career. There was a stretch in the second and third quarters that he hit only 7 of 17 passes, which BYU used to build a double-digit lead in Provo. BYU has one of the best passing defenses in college football, holding opponents to 5.5 yards per attempt, the second-best mark in the sport. And it's a concerning trend for Notre Dame's highest-profile quarterback in decades. 
        
            
                College Football Playoff Rankings reaction: Notre Dame among underrated teams slighted, SEC's efforts succeed
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Struggles vs. ranked teamsNotre Dame has breezed through largely manageable competition the past two years with Carr playing efficient football. The Fighting Irish are a combined 17-3 over the past two seasons. But when they play against the best, Carr hasn't looked the part of a first-round pick. 
Carr completes only 61% of his passes against ranked opponents and hits 6.6 yards per attempt. In unranked games, he's sitting at 69% completion and 10.0 yards per attempt. Of course, every quarterback takes a step back against tougher competition. But for Carr, the gap in production is stunning. GamesCompletion%YPGYPATDINTvs. ranked560.9%224.66.665vs. unranked1569.4%231.110.0362In games against unranked competition, Carr averages a modest 23.1 attempts per game. Notre Dame can easily lean on its running game and pull away. But in the games against ranked competition, that number jumps to 33 attempts per game, and Carr's efficiency slips dramatically. Granted, Notre Dame has other issues on offense that were exposed in Provo. The junior completed only 30% of his passes of more than 10 yards downfield and was completely outplayed by dual-threat quarterback Bear Bachmeier. The Fighting Irish receivers also struggled to create space against BYU's star defensive backs. It brings up the question: Is Carr ready to compete against elite competition at the NFL level? His early games against elite teams make the answer murky. Big opportunity aheadBy the rankings, No. 1 Miami is the best team Carr has faced in his career. But while the Hurricanes are the undisputed top team in the nation, the Hurricanes present a big opportunity for the Notre Dame passing game. Miami is absolutely stacked on offense and boasts the No. 1 rushing defense in college football. Against the pass, though, they've been gettable. The Hurricanes rank No. 122 nationally in passing defense, giving up 251.9 yards per game. With a pass rush that took a step back compared to last season, a young secondary is getting exposed. Of course, Miami's low ranking is impacted by the great rushing defense. Teams are throwing the ball with great regularity against them since running the ball is a non-starter. But even accounting for volume, Miami's passing defense has some issues, specifically, as they rank middle of the pack at 7.1 yards allowed per attempt. Last week, North Carolina's Billy Edwards Jr. completed 82% of his passes for 341 yards, four touchdowns and 10.0 yards per attempt. All of those marks were season highs. Florida State also got 298 yards and four touchdowns in a double-overtime loss to the Hurricanes. Pittsburgh quarterbacks Holden Geriner and Corey Dailey combined for 334 yards and two touchdowns. Statistically, this is one of the worst passing defenses Carr has played in his career. But with the run defense to match, the game will be on Carr's arm more than perhaps any before. Carr is rated the No. 10 overall player in the CBS Sports NFL Draft Prospect Rankings. He could become the first Notre Dame first-round quarterback since Brady Quinn in 2007, and the first top-10 pick at the position since Rick Mirer in 1993. But still, Carr was 0-2 against the two College Football Playoff teams he played last season, and 0-1 against the projected CFP participant BYU. With a less talented roster, Notre Dame won three CFP games to play for a national title just two years ago. This is the moment where Carr needs to prove he can elevate an offense. In addition to Notre Dame's season, his NFL future could take a big hit.
