title: What's next for Valkyries? Why WNBA champions could add star free agent - CBS Sports
description: After winning the WNBA title in just their second season as a franchise, the Valkyries are set up for sustained s
body:
After winning the WNBA title in just their second season as a franchise, the Valkyries are set up for sustained success
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Even as the confetti rained down from the rafters in Ballhalla, it was hard to believe that the Golden State Valkyries had actually won the 2026 WNBA title in just their second year of existence. No team in North American professional sports had ever become champions that fast, and the Valkyries did it without a single All-WNBA player -- a first in league history. "All it took was good people. That's it," Finals MVP Gabby Williams said. "All we heard last year, 'We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent.' Yeah right. We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. They don't care about scoring. They just want to play defense and rebound and do whatever it takes. We built a beautiful culture here." 
        
            
                'I stayed patient': How Finals MVP Gabby Williams made history in Game 7 to fuel Valkyries to WNBA title
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Valkyries exceeded expectations in 2025 by becoming the first expansion team to make the playoffs in their inaugural season, but even after making Williams their marquee signing in free agency last offseason, no one expected them to be title contenders. If anything, their decision to punt on the 2026 WNBA Draft by trading the No. 8 pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-rounders raised significant questions about their process. And when French center Iliana Rupert was ruled out for the season due to maternity leave, their frontcourt appeared extremely thin. And sure enough, the Valkyries got off to a middling start. As the midpoint of the season approached, the Valkyries were 10-7 and just 3-6 against teams that eventually made the playoffs. Everything changed after that point, ironically with three wins over the Atlanta Dream in the span of 11 days. Those victories were part of a nine-game winning streak that catapulted the Valkyries into the top half of the standings, where they would remain the rest of the way. They went 22-5 to close the season, and nearly chased down the Minnesota Lynx for the top seed. 
They did so on the back of one of the best defenses we have ever seen. The Valkyries' 99.1 defensive rating was more than four points per 100 possessions better than any other team, and they were second in opponent turnover rate (19.2%) and second in opponent true shooting (53.5%). Williams, who finished second to Angel Reese for Defensive Player of the Year, made the All-Defensive First Team, while Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes were All-Defensive Second Team honorees. The Valkyries' defense, combined with excellent depth and complete buy-in from everyone in the organization, helped make up for an offense that could be downright disastrous. They didn't have a single player average even 15 points per game. Their 108.2 offensive rating was seventh in the league and the second-worst among playoff teams. They were dead last in field goal percentage (42.2%) and 13th in true shooting (54%). Their inability to generate reliable offense nearly ended their season in the first round. They trailed the Dallas Wings by 16 in the second half of their winner-take-all Game 3, and had to pull off a miraculous comeback to secure the first playoff series victory in franchise history. In the semifinals, they swept the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces despite shooting 36.4% from the field, and pulled off another dramatic second-half comeback in Game 3 before winning in overtime to complete the sweep. 
The Finals was more of the same. They held the Dream to eight points in the fourth quarter of Game 1 and pulled off another late comeback despite shooting 32.1%, the third-lowest field-goal percentage in a Finals win in league history. So it went the rest of the way. In their four Finals victories, the Valkyries scored 68, 67, 64 and 68 points, respectively. In Game 7, they trailed by nine in the second half and were stuck on 32 points late in the third before Williams took over. She scored 28 of her 30 points -- tied for the most in a winner-take-all game in Finals history -- in the second half, and hit the go-ahead 3-pointer with just over two minutes to play. "[Coach Natalie Nakase] told me to stay patient. I trust her with my life," Williams said when asked what flipped in the second half of Game 7. "I stayed patient. I trusted her. She said, 'Stay patient, stay patient. The game is going to open up for you.' And it did."
"It's what we did all year," Williams added. "Just trust each other."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Season at a glanceRecord: 32-12 (No. 2 seed)Offensive rating: 108.2 (7th)Defensive rating: 99.1 (1st)Net rating: Plus-9.1 (1st)Biggest strength: DefenseThe Valkyries were one of the best defensive teams ever. They had high-end defensive talent in Williams, Burton, and Stokes, and an array of big, physical, and versatile wing players they could cycle through to maintain a high level of intensity throughout each game and the entire season. They led the league in defensive rating by a wide margin, forced turnovers at a high rate and shut down the paint. Remarkably, they held opponents to just 14 restricted-area attempts per game, 61.4% shooting on those attempts, and 31.1 points in the paint per game. Those marks all led the league.  
        
            
                Way-too-early 2027 WNBA Power Rankings: Valkyries on top; Fever, Lynx, Liberty have major offseason questions
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Biggest weakness: ScoringOn the flip side, finding consistent offense was a major issue for the Valkyries. They launched a league-record 30.3 3-point attempts per game, and when the 3s were falling, they could really pile up some points. But when they weren't, the Valkyries didn't really have any answers. In addition to their inefficient shooting, the Valkyries were last in restricted area attempts per game (14) and 12th in free throw rate (0.271), and Williams' 14.4 points per game were the second-fewest by any team's leading scorer. Key free agentsKayla Thornton (Unrestricted)Tiffany Hayes (Unrestricted)Cecilia Zandalasini (Restricted)Kaitlyn Chen (Reserved)Biggest question: Can they sign a max free agent?Weeks after the Valkyries traded the No. 8 pick on draft night, general manager Ohemaa Nyanin said the deal was made to maintain salary cap flexibility. 
"We thought we had the opportunity to potentially sign another athlete," Nyanin said at the team's media day. "My job is to make sure we maintain an understanding of what's happening today and then what could happen in the future. So the flexibility that is needed to really be able to withstand whatever could happen in the future is something I hold near and dear to me."There were plenty of rumors, particularly surrounding Napheesa Collier, but the Valkyries did not sign another max free agent alongside Williams. Now, after winning the title anyway, they will have significant cap space this winter. The official salary cap number for 2027 remains unclear due to the new revenue-sharing model, but it should be upwards of the $7 million it was in 2026. The Valkyries only have $3.2 million in guaranteed money on the books for 2027.Nyanin could very easily sign a max free agent and still have enough flexibility to fill out the rest of the roster. And there are a number of big names on the market this year, including Collier, Jackie Young, Kelsey Mitchell and Kelsey Plum. 

        
            
                WNBA free agency rankings: 10 best players available, from Napheesa Collier to Sophie Cunningham
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Collier would be the most natural fit. She's one of the most efficient scorers in the league and would provide a major boost to the Valkyries' offense without harming their defensive structure. In fact, the former Defensive Player of the Year could make the Valkyries even better on that side of the ball. Young isn't on Collier's level as a defender, but she's not a negative on that end either, and would give the Valkyries an elite offensive talent. Mitchell and Plum are arguably even better than Young on the offensive end, but are such poor defenders that the Valkyries may not be interested, no matter how much they could fix their scoring woes. The Valkyries' commitment to doing things their way has to be commended, but achieving consistent playoff success in the years to come will be difficult without more help in the scoring department. This offseason represents a unique opportunity to add a star without sacrificing any members of their core, and Nyanin's comments prior to the season showed that they are interested in acquiring a big name. But can they?
The past six months have been an advertisement for the Valkyries' culture, their rabid fan base, and the organization's commitment to excellence. In a vacuum, any player would want to be a part of this group. But in that regard, could winning the title backfire? Some players, especially stars, may not want to join the reigning champs for fear of being seen as front-runners, but it's too early to say how free agents will react. If Nyanin can convince a star to come to the Bay Area, that would be bad news for the rest of the league.WNBA Draft outlookThe Valkyries have all of their own picks (Nos. 14, 29 and 44) in the 2027 WNBA Draft, but their first-round selection at No. 14 is the only one that really matters -- certainly for 2027. Of course, that's if the Valkyries even want to make a pick. They essentially punted on the draft last season when they traded the No. 8 pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-round picks. 
If they want to keep the pick, a draft-and-stash option like French forward Aïnhoa Risacher could be an option. She's an unselfish, defense-minded player and wouldn't disrupt the team's current operations. Plus, they already have three French players on the roster.

title: Previewing a Week 10 that could reshape CFP race as biggest Saturday yet arrives - CBS Sports
description: In a season already defined by chaos, what will the most impactful regular-season weekend of the College Football
body:
In a season already defined by chaos, what will the most impactful regular-season weekend of the College Football Playoff era have in store?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Why not call college football's upcoming slate the best-ever in the College Football Playoff era?That's not hyperbole, by the way. You'll need to keep the remote close on Saturday, when the offering provides a smorgasbord of first-round-caliber matchups and enough new data points to fill a spreadsheet for the selection committee next week, after its wild first set of rankings.This is what an expanded playoff promised -- more teams with meaningful games down the stretch carrying substantial weight within the SEC, Big Ten and Big 12 title discussions, along with Notre Dame's prove-it stage against No. 1 and unbeaten Miami. The Week 10 slate features six AP top-20 matchups, tying for the most ever in AP poll history for a single weekend. Half of college football's most meaningful games left will be played Saturday, making it arguably the most impactful single day of the CFP era, which dates back to 2014.
Before glancing at the narrative-setting games, we combed through the last 15 seasons of impactful November weekends that featured stunning results that made a significant impact on the following week's playoff rankings.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin, LSU enter defining November stretch as Alabama matchup carries CFP weight
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
How will Week 10's slate stack up with some of the best since 2014?Nov. 12, 2016: No. 2 Clemson, No. 3 Michigan and No. 4 Washington were all beaten, along with No. 8 Texas A&M and No. 9 Auburn. This was during the four-team era, which shifted Ohio State from No. 5 to No. 2 and dropped Washington to No. 6. Strangely, Michigan did not budge despite a loss to Iowa.Nov. 11, 2017: Rivalry games were unkind to top-ranked Georgia (which lost to Auburn) and third-ranked Notre Dame (which got clobbered by Miami). Both the Bulldogs and Fighting Irish fell out of the top 4 while the Hurricanes and Oklahoma moved in.Nov. 5, 2022: After the initial CFP rankings released that season, No. 1 Tennessee lost to Georgia, Notre Dame climbed past fourth-ranked Clemson, and LSU toppled sixth-ranked Alabama in overtime. Georgia moved to the No. 1 spot the following week, while TCU entered the top 4.Nov. 24-25, 2017: How often have CFP Nos. 1 and 2 lost during rivalry weekend? It happened here following second-ranked Miami's upset loss to Pittsburgh on Friday night and top-ranked Alabama's setback against Auburn the next day in the Iron Bowl. The Hurricanes dropped to No. 7 while the Crimson Tide fell to No. 4. One of those teams rebounded, reached the CFP and won the national championship under the legendary Nick Saban. Looking at Saturday's appetizing menu, parity could resurface, as it has weekly this fall, for contenders aiming to strengthen their grip on coveted seeds while battling opponents with a margin for error nearing zero.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 BYU at No. 3 UtahStakes: Winner takes the driver's seat in the Big 12 Championship raceThere's nothing like a Holy War that means something nationally, and this one is particularly juiced up in Salt Lake City. BYU's trip to Utah could help determine whether the conference's three-bid playoff ambition remains realistic or deteriorates should the Utes win. That would put BYU's best-case finish at 10-2, falling short of a berth in the conference title game if Utah and Texas Tech win out. Cincinnati was supposed to be a worthy adversary for the Utes last time out, but Utah steamrolled the Bearcats after taking out the Red Raiders. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 UCLA at MinnesotaStakes: Bruins' first loss would create a three-way tie for first in the Big TenThe best way UCLA can prove the non-believers wrong is to keep winning. Nothing's been pretty the last few weeks for one of college football's three remaining unbeatens, but the Bruins are getting it done. Offensive efficiency is ranked 48th nationally right now against a favorable schedule without Nico Iamaleava at quarterback following his season-ending injury, and that's part of the reason many have tried to poke holes in this unblemished start. However, UCLA has allowed just 35 total points over its last five games, and this weekend's opponent has been offensively challenged at times, scoring only a couple of touchdowns in the season's second half. Keep it moving, Bruins -- however that may look.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Texas at No. 18 MissouriStakes: Longhorns aim for a nation-leading fourth win against ranked opponentsEli Drinkwitz must love this situation for the Tigers. No one has mentioned Missouri in the CFP race, but that'll change if it takes out the Longhorns this weekend. Texas isn't upset-proof by any means after losing at home to Florida a few weeks back and stubbing its toe against Oklahoma in Red River. Luckily for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning, the wins look good (Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss) and they're also aging well down the stretch. Texas will have the best three-loss resume of any at-large team if the Longhorns take three of their final four games.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSUStakes: Without a ranked win thus far, Lane Kiffin's back is against the CFP wall
We're not quite ready to call this one a CFP elimination game in the SEC, but it's close. Should both of these teams finish 9-3 and be within the expected SEC logjam of squads with the same record, the winner here has a leg up. And for LSU, holding potential losses to Ole Miss, Kentucky and Alabama -- all three of which could end with the same record -- that would be all she wrote. The first of three straight games against top-15 opponents for the Tigers; win two and we think LSU will be in as one of the final at-large selections. The Crimson Tide have two ranked wins (Kentucky, South Carolina), but don't have that signature victory yet. This would be it in Baton Rouge to solidify a spot as long as Alabama wins out from there.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio StateStakes: A Buckeyes loss would complicate their path to a CFP at-large berthSo much for style points. Oregon's visit to Columbus gives the two-loss Buckeyes an opportunity to steady themselves after the USC debacle, but another stumble would leave their CFP hopes dependent on considerable help from others -- and that's not where Ryan Day wants to be on Sunday. The Ducks have endured their own disappointing season, going from top-5 to unranked, but they still have enough ability to make this a nervous matchup inside the Horseshoe if Dylan Raiola plays as well as he did last week against Northwestern. Win, and Ohio State stays where it wants to be in the national picture. Lose, and the conversation shifts to the bubble for the Buckeyes.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 TennesseeStakes: Vols look to snap the Wildcats' six-game winning streak and enter the top 10
Tennessee has more to lose here despite Kentucky being the higher-ranked -- and hotter -- team. This home game carries the urgency of a playoff elimination game for Tennessee, especially with LSU still waiting on the schedule and only one ranked win (Alabama) so far. Another defeat would leave the Vols, if they win out, asking the selection committee to overlook three losses while comparing its résumé against a crowded group of at-large contenders. Kentucky's stakes are significant, too, but the Wildcats still have favorable games against Missouri, Florida and Louisville to navigate after leaving Knoxville. If Kentucky does pull this one off as a betting underdog for its seventh consecutive win, Will Stein is all but guaranteed the program's first CFP appearance unless the bottom falls out the final three games. Kentucky fans would be making reservations for the SEC Championship in Atlanta, too. For Tennessee, winning feels essential to keeping a realistic path to the bracket open in November.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole MissStakes: An Ole Miss win all but guarantees a CFP berth, while a loss could be fatal
The Rebels have wins over LSU and Missouri in their back pocket, but one that would really age well in the coming weeks is a victory over Georgia on Saturday. That's the only team with a winning record remaining for Ole Miss, which might not be in the 12-team field with a loss here and a 9-3 finish. This one's dangerous for Georgia because the guy playing quarterback for the Rebels has already thrashed this Glenn Schumann defense twice in his career. It was Trinidad Chambliss' late-game heroics that sent the Bulldogs home in the CFP quarterfinals last season, and he nearly beat Georgia between the hedges, too. Perhaps the most important factor will be the turnover battle and Pete Golding's defense doing what it can to frustrate Gunner Stockton and Georgia up front.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre DameStakes: Unbeaten and top-ranked Hurricanes hope to make things uneasy for Fighting IrishTwo of college football's most efficient teams this season go head-to-head in South Bend for a matchup that should get millions of eyes Saturday night. How good is Notre Dame when the only ranked team the Fighting Irish played this season -- BYU -- beat them in October? The same question can be asked about the Hurricanes, who held off Wake Forest in September but have since played only two opponents with winning records. Miami needed double overtime to hold Florida State on Oct. 17 and nearly lost at North Carolina last week in a lookahead spot before this one. Notre Dame swatted its only common opponent (Tar Heels) a few weeks ago and should give Miami's explosive offense -- featuring the Heisman frontrunner at quarterback -- its toughest assignment up to this point.
